changes.before: Return a fresh reading object and derive Reading using ReturnType<typeof makeReading>.
changes.after: Use `ReturnType` to describe the value a function returns.

before: ReturnType<F> extracts the result type of a function type F. In a type position, typeof makeReading gets the function’s type without calling it. Combine them to keep a Reading description tied to the actual declared function.

makeReading takes a title string and page count number and returns a new object. The shorthand {title, pages} uses those parameter values as properties; complete is true exactly when pages is zero. Reading therefore has title:string, pages:number and complete:boolean. The visible call returns an object for Maps with complete false. The type does not enforce nonnegative page counts or validate incoming JSON.
Optional local practice: Change the title at a call site and inspect which types remain unchanged.
after: `ReturnType` gets the result type of a function. In `ReturnType<typeof makeReading>`, `typeof makeReading` supplies the function's type. Neither part calls the function.
`makeReading` returns a new object with a title, a page count, and a `complete` flag. A flag is a true-or-false value. Here, `complete` is true exactly when the page count is zero.
Complete `makeReading` and define `Reading` using its return type. Return a new object each time. Keep the title and page count supplied to the function.

If the function's returned fields change, `Reading` follows their types. Here, pages must be a number; text such as `"2"` does not fit. This number type alone does not rule out negative values or check data from a file.

before.question: If makeReading’s pages parameter changes to string and its body is updated consistently, what happens to Reading.pages?
choices: ReturnType executes the function to guess the type at runtime.
It follows the changed return shape and becomes string.
before.explanation: The extracted type follows the function’s static return type, not a separate manually maintained interface.

after.question: If the function is changed so its returned pages field is text, what happens to `Reading.pages`?
choices: ReturnType runs the function to find out.
It follows the returned field and becomes text.
after.explanation: `Reading` gets its type from the function's result type. It is not a separate handwritten copy.

project.title: Reuse the return type of a function
project.task: Make `makeReading` return a new object with title, pages, and complete. Set complete to true only when pages is zero. Define `Reading` with `ReturnType<typeof makeReading>`.
project.done_when: Each call returns the right fields in a new object. Reading matches the function's result type.
